24.plain: The full test suite now runs on Windows PCs.

26.plain: Shot and sight checks skip walls they can't touch, so the server does less work.

27.plain: Player movement checks skip walls they can't touch, so the server does less work.

30.plain: Water reflections cost about a quarter less to draw, with no visible change.

32.plain: The game prepares its effects before you drop in, so the first frame of a match is about 6 times quicker.

34.plain: Slow computers no longer fail to load because of a cosmetic far-tree effect.

35.plain: The game's start-up script runs about a second faster on a Windows PC.

39.plain: The game skips painting a character model it isn't going to use.

40.plain: Two big locations build in small steps, so the match warm-up hitches less.

41.plain: The island map is painted in the background, so the page doesn't freeze while it loads.

43.plain: Sharing a link to the game now shows a proper preview card.

47.plain: Picking up items stopped creating throwaway memory: 55% less memory churn per tick.

48.plain: Loot is placed using each match's own cover walls.

57.plain: Rocket and bomb messages are always read in full, so the message after them isn't misread.

61.plain: The game stops preparing graphics it throws away, so the title shows up 4 seconds sooner on a Windows PC.

86.plain: Testers can save debug settings in the browser.

perf.name: Title screen ready, Windows Chrome (first visit)
perf.plain: The title screen now shows up 4 seconds sooner on a first visit, because the game stops preparing graphics it throws away.
perf.metric: __kr.readyAt, cold, median of 5 interleaved runs per side, [28.4-31.6] to [24.3-27.5]; settle warm-up 3908 ms to 501 ms; first match frame unchanged within noise. Metal is unmeasured

perf.name: Server work per tick
perf.plain: The server does a third less work to run each moment of a match, so one machine can host more games.
perf.metric: Real-play host tick p50 on a seeded match; results are replay-identical
perf.source: bench:host real-play scenario, before/after the three collision changes (#26, #27 and the cell-skipping ray walk that arrived with #118)

perf.name: Memory churn per tick
perf.plain: The game creates far less throwaway memory, so the computer pauses less often to clean up.
perf.metric: allocBytesPerTick on real-play; garbage collections 183 to 82, GC time 178 ms to 87 ms

perf.name: First frame of a match (processor)
perf.plain: The first moment after you drop in no longer freezes: it's about 6 times quicker.
perf.metric: First match frame, CPU step, median [851-1461] to [146-160]

perf.name: First frame of a match (graphics card)
perf.plain: The graphics card's share of that first frame went from almost half a second to a blink.
perf.metric: First match frame, GPU time, median [442-1051] to [23-47]

perf.name: Worst hitch during match warm-up
perf.plain: The biggest stutter while the island streams in is a third shorter.
perf.metric: Worst frame interval in the first 15 s, median [525-819] to [402-640]
perf.source: Before/after A/B of the change that holds a streamed location's build gate until its first draw (arrived with #118)

perf.name: Slowest 1% of warm-up frames

perf.metric: Frame interval p99 in the first 15 s
perf.source: Before/after A/B of the change that holds a streamed location's build gate until its first draw (arrived with #118)

perf.name: Start-up script, computer without a graphics card

phases.name: Safety checks for every change
phases.plain: Automatic tests that prove the game still works, on Mac, Windows and in the cloud.
phases.source: tools/ and npm test on main; open pull requests
issues: Online match test over real WebSockets
Pass/fail thresholds for the bot match and lag lab
Boot check without a graphics card
Formal models of vehicle seats and match phases
Lint rules for determinism, hot paths and URL flags
Network tail gate in npm test

phases.name: Performance
phases.plain: Measure first, then make the game and server faster, keeping only changes the numbers prove.
phases.source: tools/performance on main; open pull requests
issues: Memory at the title on a budget

phases.name: Faster loading
phases.plain: Cutting the time from opening the page to the title screen.
issues: Warm only the shaders we need
Defer far loot detail until after the title
Load the helicopter model after the title
Compile the storm and weapon effects after the title
Plan the pre-title stream by default from each device's measured time

phases.name: Memory
phases.plain: Letting 16 GB computers, and Safari in particular, play a whole match.
issues: Resource scopes and a byte ledger
Release textures' CPU copies after upload
Evict far locations once the match is in play
Texture size cap on by default
Restore the WebGL context in place

summary.plain: Since v0.2.0 the game loads on slow computers, starts each match more smoothly and costs the server less, with every change measured before and after.
